original.title: Toward a Critical Race Theory of Education
original.venue: Teachers College Record The Voice of Scholarship in Education

core_idea: Racism is ordinary and built into institutions, including schools. CRT in education examines how apparently neutral policies and practices reproduce racial inequality and centres the voices of people of colour.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: How do school policies, discipline or curriculum reproduce racial inequality?
How do students of colour experience higher education?
Typical data: counter-narratives, interviews, policy analysis.
common_mistakes: Using CRT only as a label without its tenets (permanence of racism, interest convergence, whiteness as property).
Applying US racial categories to other countries without adaptation.
Treating counter-stories as anecdotes rather than as a method with its own logic.
